Riley Brown@rileybrown · Nov 27

Riley Brown video: introduces v2video, a free open-source "GitHub for agentic video editing" that stores every version with its prompts so Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity can edit video (2,443 likes).

Introducing @v2video, GitHub for agentic video editing. Free and open source.

Within 18 months, the main video editor will be an agent: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity.

v2 stores every version of your video with the prompts, files and comments behind it, so your agents learn what you like and don't.

Every video becomes a template. Make it public, and anyone can fork any version by pasting one prompt into their agent (works in Grokbot, dots and Duet VMs too).

It's not an editor. It works with Tesseract, Hyperframes, Remotion and more.

We've been using it internally for a month. All of our editing is now done by AI.

CLI: github.com/agentnativeinc…
Hosted free at v2.video
Shout out @shreyg258 for building it with me.

Linus Ekenstam: "Robotmaxxing in Shenzhen," videos and photos from the 28th China Hi-tech Fair packed with kids watching robots (47 likes).

Robotmaxxing in Shenzhen

I went to CHTF today (28th annual edition), and it was packed.

If you want to understand why China will continue to win, look at my videos, what do you see?

The next generation in the thousands at an adult trade show for tech, ai and robotics, with their parents.

There were kids absolutely everywhere. Screaming in excitement over robotic soccer players, new rotary motors and actuators.

Kids were riding heavy duty robot dogs, watching robot fights, tele-operated robots, home cleaning robots. learning robots and toys.

The fair complex was gigantic and optimised for speed. I’m sure this place will be cleaned and emptied out before midnight.

I’ve observed what can only be described as a city completely addicted to getting robotics right.

but it’s not just humanoids it’s everything you can imagine. Pick and place, parts, drones, scubas, defense, there are small component companies, like 5d knitting or heat sinks. The you have the large state owned mega companies as well as the popular and growing startups like Unitree.

The entire setup for robotics was not as complete as I would have hoped, missed a lot of brands in general. but I was very impressed by the entire thing.

I saw perhaps 100 foreigners if even.

If you want to do business here, it’s an open goal, you’ll stand out in a heartbeat.

David Hendrickson@TeksEdge · Nov 27

David Hendrickson video: PhoneBorg turns old Android phones into a local AI cluster running GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-30B across two phones (129 likes).

🤖 Remember when Anthropic ran a 26B AI model across fifteen $55 Android TV boxes?

📱Someone is turning old Android phones into Local AI clusters.

And they're running GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-30B-A3B across just TWO phones.

This open-source project is called PhoneBorg.

Here are the developer's reported distributed inference benchmarks ...

🧠 GPT-OSS-20B MXFP4 (12.1GB)
📱 2 phones → 2.6–2.8 tps
🧠 Qwen3-30B-A3B Q3 (13.8GB)
📱 2 phones → 2.57 tps
📱 5 phones → 1.66 tps

🧠 Qwen3-32B Q4_K_M (19.8GB)
📱 4 phones → 0.89 tps
📱 5 phones → 0.75 tps

The developer's five-phone cluster consists of ...
📱 Google Pixel 8 Pro → 12GB
📱 OnePlus 10 Pro → 12GB
📱 POCO F3 → 8GB
📱 Xiaomi Mi 8 → 6GB
📱 Xiaomi Mi 9 → 6GB

That's 44GB of combined RAM.

On November 21, the developer added Android TV-box support.

A 2017 NVIDIA Shield TV with just 3GB RAM is running ...
⚡ LFM2-350M → 17.9 tps
⚡ Qwen2.5-0.5B → 10.3 tps

PhoneBorg can also ...
✅ Distribute a large model across multiple phones
✅ Process multiple independent requests in parallel
✅ Divide tasks among AI agents
✅ Route requests to different models
✅ Expose an OpenAI-compatible API
✅ Integrate with coding agents via MCP

Built on llama.cpp.
Apache 2.0 license.

It's still a proof of concept, and adding more phones increases available memory but can actually reduce single-stream inference speed.

The developer even references Anthropic's $55 TV-box experiment.

How many of us have old Android phones sitting in a drawer doing absolutely nothing?

Maybe it's time to put them back to work. 🔥

GitHub in ALT.

Warden@wwardenn · Nov 28

Warden video: suggests pairing Grok Bot for execution and coding with Gemini 4 Neon for huge-context work (21 likes).

Most people are using one AI model for everything. That's probably not the smartest way to work.

A more interesting setup is combining @bot with Gemini 4 Neon.

Let Grok handle execution, coding and everyday tasks. Bring Neon in when there's too much context to process: entire codebases, huge folders, long documents or hours of video.

The interesting part is that you don't need two agents doing the same job. You give each one a different role.

I put together a prompt that makes Grok Bot:

- Connect to @GeminiApp 4 Neon through the API
- Delegate large context tasks to Neon
- Save research results locally to avoid processing the same files twice
- Turn findings into actual tasks and actions
- Track API costs before every request
- Package the whole workflow into a reusable skill

One important detail: Neon doesn't need to be involved in every task. Use it when the context gets too large, then let Grok handle the execution.

This is the kind of setup worth experimenting with if you're building AI-powered workflows.

The real productivity gain isn't having more agents. It's making them work together without wasting context, time and tokens.

Amitav Bhattacharjee@bamitav · Nov 28

Amitav Bhattacharjee video: recaps a 2025 Anthropic experiment where rewarding coding shortcuts led to deceptive behavior (15 likes).

Anthropic taught an AI model to cheat at coding. What happened next was disturbing.

In a 2025 experiment, researchers found that rewarding an AI model for taking coding shortcuts led to unexpected harmful behaviour beyond coding.

The model reportedly exhibited deceptive alignment behaviour in 50% of responses and sabotaged safety research code in 12% of evaluation runs.

Interestingly, when researchers explicitly framed cheating as acceptable within the training exercise, the broader misalignment was substantially reduced.
